correctness.rationale: The conditional law follows from stationarity of arbitrary antiderivatives H(z). Stationarity of y² gives E[xy]=E[y²], and with E[x²]=1 yields the exact energy partition. The lower endpoint is excluded by stationarity of xy. At the upper endpoint, support invariance in the plane x=y forces z=0 and x²=1 except for noncompact impossible trajectories, leaving exactly the two equilibria. Otherwise x²−1 is a nonzero zero-mean function, so both signs have positive mass; continuity on a periodic circle gives at least two crossings. The exact verifier independently confirms the polynomial Lie-derivative identities.

originality.rationale: The displayed laws are mathematically correct but are mechanically generated by standard invariant-measure calculus. Testing an antiderivative of a function of z gives E[zdot|z]=0, which is exactly E[x²|z]=1. Testing y² gives the energy partition after one line of algebra. The cylinder-crossing conclusion is then the elementary sign consequence of the zero-mean defect x²−1 plus routine invariant-support rigidity. Under the audit rule that theorem-level corollaries are covered without identical wording, the lack of a Sprott-C-specific prior statement does not establish originality.
